raw_response:
I’m thinking about it the simple way I always do. I have 19.1 mu total, and I can’t spread myself too thin because some people in the family work outside, so I need a steady plan, not a fancy one. Wheat and maize are still my main insurance, because if cotton price is not good, grain still gives us something. I’ll keep most land in wheat-maize, about 12.1 mu, and leave 7 mu in cotton. For wheat, it is already in the ground from last autumn, so now I mainly watch water and color of the field. If the seedlings look weak or yellow, I topdress a bit more urea, same as what the better households nearby do. Maize goes in right after wheat harvest, no delay, because that summer window is very tight. Cotton I keep on less land because it takes more looking after and more picking labor, but it can still bring cash if the year is decent. I won’t spend too aggressively on inputs. I’d rather use enough fertilizer and 2 or 3 irrigations where it matters than run out of cash halfway through the season.
